Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Two names hold 74 percent of the 3,164 automated vehicles on the TxDMV report, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Waymo lists 1,259. International Transport Eng lists 7.

Both sit on one report from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, data as of October 29th. It counts 3,164 automated vehicles from 17 companies. Waymo and Tesla Robotaxi hold 74 percent of them.

Since May 28th a company running automated vehicles commercially in Texas needs a state authorization. It carries no fee and never expires.

The City of Dallas asked the department to require crash history. The department answered that the Transportation Code doesn't allow it.

A concern that an automated vehicle could cause serious bodily injury or death can go to the department's Enforcement Division. Below that standard it calls administrative enforcement unlikely.

Each car in the lot on the slides stands for ten listed vehicles.

Should lawmakers let the department require crash history?

#TxDMV #SB2807 #CityOfDallas

Notes

The record. 61 items were due for re-verification. reverify.py stamped 1, and a one-source pass stamped 28 more whose primary quote was still on its page, each with a note that states only what the source confirmed. 22 items had no source answer and 7 rest on journalism only, so they keep their earlier stamps. Two items moved and none was admitted. tx-2026-0188 gained the TxDMV Company and Vehicle Summary Report, data as of October 29th (17 companies, 3,164 automated vehicles). tx-2026-0062 gained Fort Worth's own page on the moratorium hearing scheduled for November 10th. The PUCT calendar quotes on tx-2026-0024 rolled off the feed and the PubMed pages still answer with a cookie wall, so neither was re-stamped. The instruments. Grid Watch is missing November 1st and ERCOT can't backfill it. The collector and ledger are cron's, so nothing was changed. Every other page check passed. The deck. Carousel no. 75 parks the whole roster at one stand-in car per ten listed vehicles. It ships at the round cap at 7.426 across three panel rounds (7.25, 7.386, 7.426), with no hard fail in any round. Every judge ranked frame 8 weakest. The kit person's only seated pose bakes a bowed head, so the observer reads as asleep, and three recompositions hid or lost the figure. That frame ships with its headline in attribution and Kodiak's Permian line (c68) added. Frame 5's steel rule still reads grey. The web edition for November 12th is written and bound to the same claims, with a section on who still sits up front. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:03:59 UTC and judged the session unattended (the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED was 0). It refused nothing.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
